analysis.title: Q&A with Investment Strategy: S&P 500 Enters Correction Territory
key_insights: S&P 500 is down 11.8% from its October 6 all-time high, its first correction of 2026. The shift came from optimism to anxiety over AI capex sustainability after the midterm elections, a hawkish Fed and headline risks.
VIX is at its highest level since the April/May 2025 tariff turmoil. Raymond James views further weakness as an opportunity to selectively add exposure.

Data center uncertainty: newly elected governors in Texas, Ohio and Georgia pledged to restrict or halt approvals of new data center projects. Raymond James expects projects under construction to proceed and development to shift to friendlier states.
Rates: markets price two to three more hikes by September 2027 after hot CPI and PPI. Raymond James expects one final 25 bps hike in December, the second of 2026, then an extended pause.

Cyberattacks on JPMorgan and EU agencies, plus software outages at Microsoft Outlook and air traffic control, add to anxiety. Raymond James sees the risk as manageable and a tailwind for cybersecurity spending.

Economy: GDP growth forecast of 2.3% in 2027 versus 2.4% this year, no recession in the base case. Downside risks are a data center capex slowdown and a reversed wealth effect, which Furman links to about three-tenths and seven-tenths of growth respectively.

Commodity prices, including the Bloomberg Commodity Index, have retreated from their September peak after surging on the US-Iran conflict and Russia-Ukraine supply disruptions. This should ease inflation and give the Fed flexibility.
S&P 500 targets unchanged at 7,650 year-end and 8,450 at 12 months, implying about 23% upside. Strategists elsewhere are cutting targets after raising them near 8,000.

Four supports for the equity view: no recession, Q3 EPS up 31% YoY with 2027 consensus EPS growth of 16%, forward P/E compressed from 22.2x to 16.6x, and oversold signals (put/call at highest since April, 14-day RSI at 29).
Technology is down 24.7% from its October 6 high, in bear market territory. Raymond James calls the decline disconnected from fundamentals.
AI demand evidence: hyperscaler cloud revenue +63% YoY in Q3 versus 54% in Q2, cloud backlogs +141% to $1.8 trillion, and 57% of businesses use AI per Ramp versus 44% a year ago.
Tech 2027 earnings are projected up 43% versus 16% for the S&P 500. Tech trades at a discount to the S&P for the first time since 2019 and semiconductors are at their lowest forward P/E since 2011.

Emerging risk: falling tech share prices raise equity financing costs and could create a self-reinforcing cycle that constrains AI investment. No funding stress is seen so far, and Anthropic's recent IPO suggests healthy appetite.

Bonds: yields fell across the curve in a flight to quality, restoring Treasuries as a diversifier. The GS Financial Conditions Index is at its highest since May 2025 and HY spreads are 344 bps. The firm favors up-in-quality credit and keeps a 4.50%-4.75% 12-month 10-year target.

sector_views.rationale: Selloff is seen as disconnected from fundamentals, with 2027 earnings growth of 43%, a valuation discount to the S&P 500 and strong AI demand backlogs.
Data center slowdown could reduce demand for equipment and services tied to the buildout.
Up-in-quality credit bias and Treasuries diversifying equity risk.

earnings_insights: Q3 S&P 500 EPS reported up 31% YoY.
2027 consensus S&P 500 EPS growth estimate is 16%, more than double the historical average, after upward revisions.
2027 Technology sector EPS growth consensus estimate is 43%, nearly three times the S&P 500's expected 16%.
Hyperscaler cloud revenue reported +63% YoY in Q3 versus +54% in Q2 2026, with cloud backlogs +141% to $1.8 trillion.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Raymond James forecast, only modestly below 2.4% this year, so no recession base case.
This year's pace as cited by the bank, the baseline for the 2027 slowdown.
Bank expects a hike followed by an extended pause, less than the two to three more hikes priced by September 2027.
Market pricing the bank believes overestimates tightening.
Reaffirmed target, supported by cooling inflation and less Fed tightening than priced.
Spreads widened on growth concerns and weaker sentiment.

risk_factors: Further data center capex slowdown from state regulation and higher developer borrowing costs.
Negative wealth effect from falling equity and home values weighing on affluent consumer spending.
Further Fed tightening on sticky core inflation.
Tech selloff raising equity financing costs and constraining AI investment.
Tighter financial conditions and credit spread widening.

geopolitical: US-Iran conflict and Russia-Ukraine war drove supply disruptions and commodity surges through 2026.
Tariffs and the Iran conflict cited as earlier challenges, with equity volatility subdued until recently.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud revenue +63% YoY, backlogs of $1.8 trillion, 57% business AI adoption and 2027 tech EPS growth of 43% support a durable capital investment cycle.
tension_points.bear_case: State restrictions on data centers, higher developer borrowing costs and a falling tech share price raising equity financing costs could stall the buildout and weigh on growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Signs of funding stress among major technology companies, which the report says have not yet appeared.

tension_points.bull_case: One final 25 bps hike in December then a pause, helped by falling commodity prices and tighter financial conditions.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets price two to three more hikes by September 2027 after sticky core CPI and PPI and hawkish Fed commentary.
